insight.title: Why some products get better as more people use them
insight.subtitle: A look at how network effects shape our daily lives

sections.text: Imagine you owned the very first telephone ever made. It would be completely useless because you had nobody to call. The value of a single phone is zero. However, when your friend gets one, the device gains value. Every new person who joins makes your own tool much more powerful.

This concept is called a network effect. It explains why apps like WhatsApp or platforms like eBay are so dominant. People go where everyone else already is. This creates a massive advantage for big companies. The more users they have, the harder it is for a new competitor to win.

These invisible loops shape our digital world today. They turn small ideas into global giants quickly. While these networks offer great convenience, they also lead to monopolies. Understanding this helps us see why we stick with certain services, even when better options appear. It is all about the crowd's connection.
